system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for London, United Kingdom. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in London itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent London space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Mayfair, East End, South London, West End/Soho) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several London spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in London, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: White Cube
galleries.note: London-born powerhouse with a museum-calibre programme, blue-chip roster and commanding global fair presence.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.note: A defining global mega-gallery whose London exhibitions regularly attract major institutional and market attention.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth
galleries.note: Internationally dominant gallery combining major living artists, estates, scholarship and institutional-scale exhibitions.

galleries.name: David Zwirner
galleries.note: Globally influential programme spanning canonical contemporary artists, major estates and critically prominent new work.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery
galleries.note: Historic international gallery representing leading postwar and contemporary artists, with exceptional institutional reach.

galleries.name: Lisson Gallery
galleries.note: A foundational London gallery for conceptualism, minimalism and ambitious international contemporary practice.

galleries.name: Victoria Miro
galleries.note: Highly respected programme with influential painters, photographers and installation artists and sustained museum recognition.

galleries.name: Sadie Coles HQ
galleries.note: Agenda-setting gallery known for rigorous exhibitions and a roster central to British and international contemporary art.

galleries.name: Serpentine Galleries
galleries.note: Internationally influential public galleries commissioning major exhibitions, architecture and interdisciplinary cultural projects.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac
galleries.note: Major European gallery presenting historically significant postwar figures and globally prominent contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Whitechapel Gallery
galleries.note: Landmark public gallery with a long record of introducing consequential modern and contemporary artists to London.

galleries.name: Sprüth Magers
galleries.note: Critically rigorous international gallery representing major conceptual, feminist and media-based practices.

galleries.name: Thomas Dane Gallery
galleries.note: Highly regarded programme linking leading British artists with important international and moving-image practices.

galleries.name: Maureen Paley
galleries.note: Pioneering East End gallery instrumental in developing generations of critically important artists.

galleries.name: Stephen Friedman Gallery
galleries.note: Established international gallery with a strong record in painting, sculpture and artists from the African diaspora.

galleries.name: Pilar Corrias
galleries.note: Influential programme of internationally recognised artists, particularly strong in painting and conceptually driven installation.

galleries.name: Institute of Contemporary Arts
galleries.note: Historically vital experimental institution supporting contemporary art, film, performance and countercultural debate.

galleries.name: Goodman Gallery
galleries.note: Landmark African-founded gallery with a politically engaged roster and deep international institutional influence.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.note: Globally prominent gallery whose London branch extends a high-profile international programme and market network.

galleries.name: Alison Jacques
galleries.note: Critically distinguished gallery combining influential contemporary artists with major rediscovered artists and estates.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler
galleries.note: Leading European gallery with a formidable roster across painting, sculpture and conceptually ambitious practice.

galleries.name: Michael Werner Gallery
galleries.note: Historically important gallery renowned for postwar European art and intellectually demanding contemporary painting.

galleries.name: Modern Art
galleries.note: Stuart Shave's influential gallery supports prominent international artists with a distinctive, critically followed programme.

galleries.name: Camden Art Centre

galleries.name: Chisenhale Gallery

galleries.name: South London Gallery

galleries.name: Herald St

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin
galleries.note: International gallery noted for institutionally prominent, multidisciplinary artists and substantial global reach.

galleries.name: David Kordansky Gallery
galleries.note: Important American gallery whose permanent London space brings a highly regarded international roster to the city.

galleries.name: Timothy Taylor

galleries.name: Frith Street Gallery

galleries.name: Pippy Houldsworth Gallery

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: International gallery with significant market influence across contemporary painting and established postwar art.

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo

galleries.name: Skarstedt

galleries.name: Gasworks

galleries.name: Kate MacGarry

galleries.name: The Approach

galleries.name: Carlos/Ishikawa

galleries.name: Emalin

galleries.name: Studio Voltaire

galleries.name: Cabinet

galleries.name: greengrassi

galleries.name: Hollybush Gardens

galleries.name: Corvi-Mora

galleries.name: Lévy Gorvy Dayan

galleries.name: GRIMM

galleries.name: Hales Gallery

galleries.name: Arcadia Missa

galleries.name: Project Native Informant

galleries.name: Union Pacific

galleries.name: Josh Lilley

galleries.name: Edel Assanti

galleries.name: Maximillian William

galleries.name: Tiwani Contemporary

galleries.name: Raven Row

galleries.name: The Showroom

galleries.name: Richard Saltoun Gallery

galleries.name: Saatchi Yates

galleries.name: Kristin Hjellegjerde Gallery

galleries.name: Niru Ratnam
